statement: ALTER TABLE orders ADD COLUMN note TEXT NULL
why: Without ALGORITHM=INSTANT, MySQL silently falls back to a table rebuild if the change does not qualify.
fix: Add ALGORITHM=INSTANT so an ineligible change fails instead of rebuilding.

statement: ALTER TABLE orders ADD COLUMN status INT NOT NULL
why: A second ALTER on `orders` in the same migration takes another metadata lock and may rebuild twice.
fix: Combine the changes into one ALTER TABLE, or split them into separate migrations.

statement: ALTER TABLE orders ADD COLUMN status INT NOT NULL
why: Without ALGORITHM=INSTANT, MySQL silently falls back to a table rebuild if the change does not qualify.
fix: Add ALGORITHM=INSTANT so an ineligible change fails instead of rebuilding.

statement: ALTER TABLE orders ADD COLUMN status INT NOT NULL
why: NOT NULL with no DEFAULT makes MySQL fill existing rows with an implicit value (0, '', ...) that the schema never states.
fix: Add the column as NULL, backfill, then tighten later; or get the default approved explicitly.

statement: ALTER TABLE orders ADD COLUMN flag INT NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, ALGORITHM=INSTANT, LOCK=NONE
why: A second ALTER on `orders` in the same migration takes another metadata lock and may rebuild twice.
fix: Combine the changes into one ALTER TABLE, or split them into separate migrations.

statement: ALTER TABLE orders ADD COLUMN flag INT NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, ALGORITHM=INSTANT, LOCK=NONE
why: ALGORITHM=INSTANT does not accept a LOCK clause; MySQL rejects the statement.
fix: Remove the LOCK clause.

statement: ALTER TABLE orders ADD COLUMN flag INT NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, ALGORITHM=INSTANT, LOCK=NONE
why: NOT NULL on an existing table needs a permanent default, and the default becomes part of the schema.
fix: Add the column as NULL, backfill, then tighten later; or get the default approved explicitly.

statement: ALTER TABLE orders MODIFY COLUMN note VARCHAR(10), ADD PRIMARY KEY (id)
why: A second ALTER on `orders` in the same migration takes another metadata lock and may rebuild twice.
fix: Combine the changes into one ALTER TABLE, or split them into separate migrations.

statement: ALTER TABLE orders MODIFY COLUMN note VARCHAR(10), ADD PRIMARY KEY (id)
why: Changing column `note` usually rebuilds the table and is not INSTANT.
fix: Use expand/contract: add a new column, backfill, switch readers, drop the old one.

statement: ALTER TABLE orders MODIFY COLUMN note VARCHAR(10), ADD PRIMARY KEY (id)
why: Changing the primary key rebuilds the whole table.
fix: Use an online schema change tool on a shadow table.

statement: ALTER TABLE orders DROP COLUMN legacy, RENAME COLUMN a TO b
why: A second ALTER on `orders` in the same migration takes another metadata lock and may rebuild twice.
fix: Combine the changes into one ALTER TABLE, or split them into separate migrations.

statement: ALTER TABLE orders DROP COLUMN legacy, RENAME COLUMN a TO b
why: Column `legacy` is dropped or renamed: cheap for MySQL, but application versions still running read the old name.
fix: Deploy code that no longer uses the column first (contract phase), then drop or rename.

statement: ALTER TABLE orders DROP COLUMN legacy, RENAME COLUMN a TO b
why: Column `a` is dropped or renamed: cheap for MySQL, but application versions still running read the old name.
fix: Deploy code that no longer uses the column first (contract phase), then drop or rename.

statement: ALTER TABLE orders ADD INDEX idx_a (a), ADD CONSTRAINT fk FOREIGN KEY (p) REFERENCES parent (id)
why: A second ALTER on `orders` in the same migration takes another metadata lock and may rebuild twice.
fix: Combine the changes into one ALTER TABLE, or split them into separate migrations.

statement: ALTER TABLE orders ADD INDEX idx_a (a), ADD CONSTRAINT fk FOREIGN KEY (p) REFERENCES parent (id)
why: A secondary index is built in place, but replicas apply it serially and can lag on a large table.
fix: Check replica lag during the build; for very large tables use an online schema change tool.

statement: ALTER TABLE orders ADD INDEX idx_a (a), ADD CONSTRAINT fk FOREIGN KEY (p) REFERENCES parent (id)
why: Adding a foreign key can take long locks and validates existing rows; gh-ost cannot run on tables with foreign keys.
fix: Prefer pt-online-schema-change for tables with foreign keys, and check the parent key is unique.

statement: ALTER TABLE orders ENGINE=InnoDB, ALGORITHM=COPY
why: A second ALTER on `orders` in the same migration takes another metadata lock and may rebuild twice.
fix: Combine the changes into one ALTER TABLE, or split them into separate migrations.

statement: ALTER TABLE orders ENGINE=InnoDB, ALGORITHM=COPY
why: ALGORITHM=COPY rebuilds the whole table and blocks writes while it runs.
fix: Use an online schema change tool, or an expand/contract migration.

statement: DELETE FROM orders
why: UPDATE or DELETE with no WHERE touches every row in one transaction: long locks, huge undo log, replica lag.
fix: Move the data change to a batched backfill (keyset pagination, throttled).

statement: UPDATE orders SET a = 1
why: UPDATE or DELETE with no WHERE touches every row in one transaction: long locks, huge undo log, replica lag.
fix: Move the data change to a batched backfill (keyset pagination, throttled).
